knowledge.decision: Which visible action should receive primary emphasis now?
distinctions: A supporting responsibility is not automatically a separate action context
Danger communicates consequence; primary communicates current task emphasis
forbidden: Assign a primary action mechanically to every visual region
Determine emphasis from verbs such as create, query, save, or submit alone
knowledge.guidance: Treat high emphasis as a scarce signal within the current action context. Use zero or one primary CTA when the brief and task state imply a clear next action; keep supporting actions lower emphasis. A clearly separated temporary task surface may have its own primary action. Infer emphasis from intent and consequences, never from the action verb alone.
optional: Use no primary CTA when the task has no clearly dominant next action
Allow a clearly separated temporary task surface to have its own primary action
required: Identify the current action context before assigning primary emphasis
Ensure an emphasized action meaningfully advances or commits the current task

avoidWhen: the surface has no explicit action
useWhen: a page or region presents multiple possible actions

records.summary: Emphasize the action that advances the current primary intent without inventing rigid decision domains.
records.title: Action Emphasis by Current Intent

knowledge.decision: Does the action target selected rows, one row, or the list itself?
distinctions: Popconfirm confirms an action but does not define its scope
forbidden: Bulk semantics for create, refresh, or single-row edit
knowledge.guidance: Use a bulk action surface only when a non-empty multi-row selection is the explicit target.

useWhen: distinguish multi-select action from row or global action

records.summary: Choose action scope from the current selection rather than visual proximity to a table.
records.title: Bulk versus Row Actions

knowledge.decision: Does this setting alter what the Table displays or which records the query returns?
distinctions: Tree/Checkbox may serve column hierarchy; TreeSelect may choose filter values but does not define ownership
forbidden: Store query values in column metadata
knowledge.guidance: Visibility, fixed position, and order belong to column settings; field enablement, operators, and defaults belong to filter configuration.

useWhen: distinguish column display from search criteria

records.summary: Separate table presentation configuration from query configuration.
records.title: Column Settings versus Filters

knowledge.decision: Which filters should be enabled and initialized?
distinctions: Filter defaults affect returned records; column defaults affect presentation
knowledge.guidance: Keep enabled fields, operators, and supplied defaults explicit and reversible. Prototype changes remain in memory unless the page provides a separately approved persistence flow.

records.summary: Define enabled search fields, valid operators, and safe default values.
records.title: Filter Defaults and Operators

knowledge.decision: Does this form need a single continuous page or explicit stages?
distinctions: Strong signals create stages; supporting signals only increase cognitive load
forbidden: Choose Steps only because the form has many fields
knowledge.guidance: Default to a grouped single page. Use stages when users can understand real dependency, validation, handoff, irreversibility, or risk boundaries. Size, duration, and resumption only support that decision.
optional: Use anchors, drafts, recovery, and error location for long continuous forms
required: Identify meaningful stage boundaries before choosing Steps

avoidWhen: the interaction is not a form
useWhen: choosing how to present a business document form

records.summary: Choose a staged form from meaningful task boundaries, not size alone.
records.title: Single-page versus Staged Form
